title: Count Distinct Subarrays Divisible by K in Sorted Array
summary: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-descending order and a positive integer k, count the number of distinct subarrays whose sum is divisible by k.
statement: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-descending order and a positive integer k, count the number of distinct subarrays whose sum is divisible by k. Two subarrays are considered distinct if they contain different sequences of values.
constraints: nums is a sorted nondecreasing array of up to 100,000 positive integers.
A subarray is good when its sum is divisible by positive k.
Count distinct value sequences rather than distinct index intervals.
hints: Ordinary prefix remainders count good index intervals, so only duplicate value sequences need correction.
In a sorted array, a repeated subarray sequence can occur at multiple positions only when it consists of one repeated value.
Count all divisible intervals, then for each equal-value run and qualifying length h subtract runLength-h duplicate copies.
Every nonconstant sorted sequence has a unique boundary location, while each constant sequence is thereby reduced to one count.
editorial: Every nonconstant sorted sequence has a unique boundary location, while each constant sequence is thereby reduced to one count.

tests.explanation: The distinct good sequences are [1,2], [3], and [1,2,3].
Only lengths three and six form distinct divisible sequences, so the answer is two.
